title: Recommendations to achieve 5 stars
body:
In my opinion this is a truly wonderful app. It has a one off payment that is much cheaper than any other apps like it with memberships, and it gives you a great amount of features.

Here are a few recommendations to turn this 4-star rating into a solid 5:
1) The ability to pause habits needs to be added, as people can’t do all their habits if they are travelling/on a holiday, etc.
2) A cool little feature you could add is being able to change when a new day starts. This is very helpful for people who stay up late, because it means I can tick habits off even if it is past 12:00am.
3) A big feature that has to be added is being able to track bad habits. E.g. if someone has a smoking habit they can track how many times they smoke a day, and the less the better.
4) I noticed a small error in text. If I allow multiple checkins per day on a habit and then select ‘1 time’, it says on the habit screen ‘1 times per day’ instead of ‘1 time per day’. Just a little grammatical error I thought I’d make the developers aware of.

I really hope the developers see this review, and if you do, I want to thank you for this amazing app. For its price I think it surpasses other apps in this field, such as Productivity or Streaks. I know you are all working very hard to perfect this app, but please address the issues I have presented above, as it would make me and countless other users ecstatic.

Edit: Thanks for responding. I can’t wait to see the big updates in the future. I just want to address one more issue with the UI of this app. It would be much more motivating if you could see your streak without the need to swipe up. It would be neat if you could also see the streak of each habit on the page where you can see all your habits, instead of just seeing the number of checkins for the day. Thank you once again for reading reviews and responding. I’ll be sure to change my rating to 5 stars when the updates come out!

title: Beautiful and motivating
body:
I love this app. It's incredibly customisable, and looks gorgeous. 

I'm a very visual person, so the combination of large pictures and colourful calendars/graphs is great. I really feel motivated to tick things off, more than any other habit app. 

Apart from the couple of things I'd like to see (that I'll mentioned next), I really can't fault this app. It's amazing. 

As for suggestions:

Edit: This has been included!
• Some way of recording habits that you do more than once a day (e.g. brushing teeth morning and night). At the moment I'm just creating two habits, but it'd be nice to be able to condense it into one. 

• Speaking of condensing: Categories (e.g. Health, Skills, etc.). This would be useful if you've got lots of habits for different areas of life (like me), and want to briefly view one 'area'. 

Edit: This has been included!
• Multiple notifications per day. For example, if you're wanting to drink water throughout the day, or do a habit both day and night.

The free version allows you all the access you need to see if it meets your needs, if it does the price is eminently reasonable.

Only tiny quibble is that the intro video goes a bit too fast for me. Overall nigh-on indispensable for me.

title: Most motivational habit tracker in the store!
body:
I scoured the appstore for habit apps, wanting to see if an app would help with achieving done goals. I eventually downloaded about 12 to try - note that some apps don't let you try it out without forking out at all so the in-app upgrade was a good option allowing me to see the apps potential (the only alternative being releasing a free demo version separately).

As I tried them all out I kept coming back to this one, eventually narrowing it down to 5 apps with the functionality that suited me. I can't believe some apps out there have a yearly subscription circa £30, though I would have considered it if it did everything I wanted (but they didn't!). I am pleased to support good development and invest in apps that make a difference in my life, and this one is a steal at £5 as far as I'm concerned. 

If others are looking for an app to build new or persevere with existing habits, I can't recommend this enough. If you need one that allows you to track bad habits in order to give something up then this app doesn't really facilitate that at the time of writing this review, although that wasn't a requirement for me. 

Being a very visual person (like other reviewers here), flicking through the cards with images I've chosen for myself to 'advertise' my goal is really motivating and almost introduces a type of gamification to the whole process. It's immediately one of my most frequently opened apps and makes me do a task to get it ticked off, which is just the effect I was after.

I look forward to seeing where the developers take this app. They've been quick to respond to my suggestions and feedback so I'm keen to see what they do in the reporting side, which is a small weakness now (I only stumbled on the charts in the profile section by accident!) It'd be great to have charts to show cumulative effort and consistency, and compare progress of habits in the same view. I would also enjoy a dashboard view like the excellent notification widget shows. However the essence of the app is in the uncluttered separate screen per habit construction which really makes this app. Simple but so powerful. 

Well done neybox!

title: Great app!
body:
I rarely write reviews but the negative ones here annoyed me - yes, it's a paid app with a free trial. Would you pay £4 for an app without testing it first? 
How is that a surprise when it says so on the main page of the app? Good software cannot be free.

The app is very well designed. It does what I wanted it to - helps me keep track of habits I want to develop. The addition of cards which let you create little motivation boards was what made me pay for the full version. 

I didn't realize I wanted the motivation boards but they made all the difference - let's say you want to run in the mornings. You've barely got enough motivation to sit up and grab your phone. Leaving your bed seems impossible. You launch the app, see the cover of your running habit, scroll down and look through pictures of how you'll look like if you stick with the habit, the data on how long you've been running, your weight graph. Now you want to go running.

Guys, stop complaining about freemium / in-app purchases, the App Store allows no demos so that's the only way! You should be glad you get developers who spend hours developing stuff you can use for free if you want to. And it makes perfect sense to pay once you feel the app delivers value. 4£ is a bargain if it ends up changing your life/habits.

Would be great to have a Mac and iPad version too.

I have to add though...you've obviously been heavily "inspired" by Momentum (another habit app) right? 🤔 I mean...look at those icon colours...if your app is a success you'll have to send its developer a big box of chocolate at least.
